Ovarian carcinoma (largely high-grade serous) often presents at an advanced stage: complex, solid-cystic adnexal masses, often bilateral, with peritoneal spread.
CT signs of peritoneal carcinomatosis: ascites, peritoneal thickening and nodularity, "omental cake" (plaque-like infiltrated omentum), implants on the liver capsule, diaphragm, mesentery and pouch of Douglas; retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
The report should describe the sites that determine cytoreductive surgery: diaphragm, hepatic hilum, small bowel mesentery, bowel serosa, lymph nodes above the celiac trunk. This guides the choice between primary surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
Differential diagnosis: ovarian metastases (Krukenberg) from stomach or colon, lymphoma, primary peritoneal carcinoma; among benign lesions, tubo-ovarian abscesses and endometriomas, which however do not cause carcinomatosis.
